inputs.original_text: They’re presenting Mary Ngechi Ngethe as the convenient end of the story: unsuitable cemetery land bought for Ksh.283 million, and the money supposedly recovered from her. That doesn’t answer who shaped the wider procurement process or who else may have benefited. A single committee chair taking the blame—and a claim that the money was “recovered”—could be exactly what makes the public stop asking questions. The tidy ending deserves more suspicion, not less.
inputs.modified_text: They want everyone to see Mary Ngechi Ngethe as the whole story: unsuitable cemetery land bought for Ksh.283 million, with the money supposedly “recovered.” But a neat recovery claim and one committee chair to blame don’t explain who shaped the procurement or who else stood to benefit. That tidy ending looks less like accountability than a way to shut down the questions that matter.
